environment.description: Same Spring Boot application deployed in an AWS account (OU: ou-prod-restricted) where the organizational SCP 'DenyDangerousIAMActions' (p-xk82mf9a) applies a blanket Deny on iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:PutUserPolicy, iam:CreateUser, iam:DeleteUser, iam:AttachRolePolicy for all principals except the break-glass role (arn:aws:iam::*:role/BreakGlassAdmin). Additionally, the application's IAM role has a permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::111222333444:policy/AppServiceBoundary) that explicitly denies iam:* and sts:AssumeRole on any resource outside the application's own service namespace. The effective permission set means even if CSRF triggers the controller action, the downstream IAM API calls (assignRole → iam:AttachUserPolicy, deleteUser → iam:DeleteUser) will return AccessDenied. CloudTrail logs show these denied calls are alerted on via EventBridge → SNS within 30 seconds.

config.scp_effect: Deny on iam:AttachUserPolicy, iam:PutUserPolicy, iam:CreateUser, iam:DeleteUser, iam:AttachRolePolicy for all principals except arn:aws:iam::*:role/BreakGlassAdmin
config.permission_boundary: arn:aws:iam::111222333444:policy/AppServiceBoundary - Deny iam:*, Deny sts:AssumeRole except own namespace
config.monitoring: CloudTrail → EventBridge rule on AccessDenied for iam:* → SNS alert
